previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and constipation lasting over a week. She had no active gastrointestinal bleeding, but her symptoms were likely exacerbated by severe constipation. Imaging revealed volume overload with bilateral pleural effusions and subcutaneous edema, consistent with acute on chronic diastolic heart failure. Her hypertension was managed with re-initiation of home medications, and her blood pressure stabilized. A urinary tract infection was suspected due to elevated white count and positive urinalysis; treatment was adjusted after urine culture showed yeast colonization. An aggressive bowel regimen resolved constipation, and she remained nausea-free after admission. Her renal function improved slightly, and electrolyte imbalances from diuresis were corrected. She was discharged back to extended care with medication adjustments, including increased metolazone and addition of Bisacodyl, and plans to address depression through rehab services.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure

have significant complaint of nausea but no episode sof emesis

what appeared to be a scab at the site of her recent CABG with 
some skin breakdown next to the scab.  CT surg was contacted who 
felt this was an eschar.  Wound debridement was performed and a 
wound vac was placed.  Vancomycin was initially started 
empirically, wound cultures were negative but CT surg wanted to 
continue po antibiotics for a period of 2 weeks.  Prior to 
transport to rehab the wound vac was removed and wet-to-dry 
dressing was placed.  The wound vac will need to be replaced 
once she arrives to rehab and changed every 3 days.  The patient 
is to follow up with CT surg as an outpatient 2 weeks after 
discharge and continue augmentin until that time.

intake plus increasing creatinine suspicious for prerenal ARF.

re-hydrated with D5W.  This improved by discharge.

initially held due to concerns for ARF.  She did not appear 
fluid overloaded on exam or chest xray.  She was cautiously 
repleted with IVF and she did not manifest any signs of CHF 
exacerbation.

metoprolol as well as her clonidine patch as she was refusing 
her po BP meds.  Her BP was very difficult to control on this 
regimen.  As she began to tolerate po her home doses of 
hydralazine and amlodipine were restarted.  On the day of 
discharge her lasix and metolazone were restarted and the oral 
metoprolol were restarted.  She will need to have her 
electrolytes rechecked at rehab.

but the patient was persistently hypokalemic despite repeat 
repletion.  On her admission medication list she appears to have 
been getting IV KCl repletion at rehab.  This was not added to 
her discharge medication list - but she will need to have repeat 
electrolytes especially with restarting her lasix and will 
likely need KCl on a regular basis.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with coronary artery disease, status post CABG
in ___ with recent urinary tract infection.  Now with nausea, vomiting,
diarrhea, and abdominal pain for the past four days.  Assess for colitis or
perforation.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axially acquired images were obtained from the lung bases to the
pubic symphysis without IV contrast due to patient's renal function.  Coronal
and sagittal reformatted images were also displayed.

FINDINGS:

CT OF THE ABDOMEN:  Please note there is some artifact due to patient's
contact with the bore on the left side of her body.  The left-sided
subcutaneous tissues are excluded from view.  There is a trace left-sided
pleural effusion which has decreased in size since the previous study.  The
right-sided pleural effusion has resolved.  Minimal dependent atelectasis is
noted at the left lung base.

The non-contrast appearance of the spleen, adrenal glands, kidneys, pancreas,
gallbladder, and liver are within normal limits.  There is a small hiatal
hernia.  The stomach is otherwise normal.

There is no free air or free fluid.

Fat stranding surrounds the proximal ascending colon and cecum with associated
marked colonic wall thickening.  The appendix demonstrates secondary
inflammatory changes from the ascending colon. Additional wall thickening of
the transverse colon is likely given adjacent mesenteric fat stranding,
although evaluation is more limited given bowel collapse. 

CT OF THE PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST:  The rectum is within normal limits.  A
Foley catheter is placed within the bladder.  Small foci of air is likely due
to recent instrumentation.  Multiple calcifications are noted within the
uterus, consistent with calcified fibroids.  There is no free fluid.  There is
no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

BONE WINDOWS:  No concerning osseous lesions are identified.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Marked wall thickening of the cecum and the proximal ascending colon with
adjacent fat stranding consistent with colitis. Additional wall thickening of
the transverse colon is likely given adjacent mesenteric fat stranding,
although evaluation is more limited given bowel collapse. Patient may be
progressing to a pancolitis. Given history of antibiotic use, strongly
consider C. difficile infection. 

2.  Largely resolved pleural effusions with only residual trace left pleural
effusion remaining.
